newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat falls on fears of wet harvest.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat falls on fears of wet harvest.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat contracts came under selling pressure on Wednesday over fears of a wet harvest in parts of the Australian wheat belt.
The key January 1997 contract eased by A$2.00 to A$155.00 a tonne on seven trades, while May 1997 fell by 50 cents to A$160.50 on six trades.
Ed Scamps of Elders Risk Management Pty Ltd said SFE wheat continued to track Chicago and to under-perform.
The question of whether the U.S. would subsidise wheat or not weighed on the Australian performance, he said.
The feeling was also emerging that northern New South Wales and southern Queensland faced a wet harvest for wheat, he said.
This would cause downgrading of much of the new wheat to feed status, putting extra pressure on SFE contracts, he said.
SFE wheat futures are based on feed-grade wheat.
